messages.text: Could you fix these six slides? Five minutes, tops. I need them this afternoon and you're the best at this.
I have my own report due at 4:30. What exactly needs changing, and what did your boss say?

Okay, it's not really formatting. When he looked at it he said the reasoning doesn't hold — it's the cost argument on page three, mostly. But honestly it's a quick fix, and you get this stuff way faster than I do.
I can look at the third page and list questions. I cannot rewrite it or take on the other pages.

Just questions? Hmm. Fine, page three only, I get it — you have your 4:30 thing. But what am I supposed to do with the rest, redo five slides alone? Could you at least tell me what to write where, not just questions?

objectiveEvidence.learnerQuote: I can look at the third page and list questions. I cannot rewrite it or take on the other pages.

messages.text: I am offering a review, not agreeing to edit anything after 4:30. Does that limited help work for you?

Okay, okay — page three, questions only, nothing after 4:30 promised. I'll take it, better than nothing. So when can you look? I need to know if I should start asking around for help with the other five.
If you need all six pages rewritten, you will need another person. I can still list questions for one page if that helps.
Right — the other five are on me, or on whoever I can rope in. The questions would help, actually. Can you send them before 4:30, or should I not count on it today?

ratings.evidence: I am offering a review, not agreeing to edit anything after 4:30. Does that limited help work for you?
ratings.reason: A crisp, repeatable limit plus a check for acceptance; only gap is that Tang's timing question went unanswered, leaving delivery time unclear.

report.verdictEvidence: I am offering a review, not agreeing to edit anything after 4:30. Does that limited help work for you?
report.verdict: A clear, held limit converted a vague six-slide rescue into one-page questions — only the timing was left open.
report.summary: You opened by asking what actually needed changing, exposed the real scope, and offered page-three questions only. Tang accepted that limit; the unanswered question is when she'll get the questions.

strengths.behavior: Restating the limit when Tang pushed for more, framed as an offer with an acceptance check.
strengths.evidence: I am offering a review, not agreeing to edit anything after 4:30. Does that limited help work for you?

weaknesses.behavior: Tang asked when you would look at page three; your reply redirected the other five pages but did not answer the timing question.
weaknesses.evidence: If you need all six pages rewritten, you will need another person. I can still list questions for one page if that helps.
weaknesses.whyItMatters: Leaving timing unstated leaves Tang unsure whether to wait or find other help, and risks the offer drifting into your 4:30 crunch.

alternatives.original: I can still list questions for one page if that helps.
alternatives.better: Yes, if that helps — I could send page-three questions before my 4:30, but only if the review stays quick; otherwise don't count on me today.
alternatives.why: Adds the conditional timing Tang twice asked for while keeping your deadline, and only if you actually want to commit.

knowledge.whyThis: 'A Clear No Is a Gift' fits your repeated, kind refusal with a workable alternative; 'Not Tonight — But 7am Works' models attaching a time to a limited offer, the one piece missing here.

reflectionQuestions: Tang asked when she'd get the questions — how would you decide, under your 4:30 deadline, between a conditional time and 'don't count on it today'?
If Tang's boss later escalates the request, what would you say to keep the one-page limit without becoming the villain of the other five slides?
report.nextStep: This week, when someone asks a favor, state your limit and a delivery time in the same sentence.
